notes: Alentejo wines taste young, fruity or floral when new, and develop more complex aromas with age.
Reds range from ruby to deep red, and whites from pale lemon to light gold.
Some wine is still made in large clay pots called talhas, a tradition dating back to Roman times.

blurb.text: The DOC for eight subregions of the Alentejo, the large southern region that covers about a third of mainland Portugal and is also noted for cork. Some producers still make wine in clay pots, a practice that goes back to Roman times. Allowed grapes include Alicante Bouschet, Trincadeira, Aragonez and Antão Vaz.
